model.name: Alias / Same-as Mapping
model.purpose: Provide a reusable, format-neutral mixin that lets any subject model assert, qualify and govern equivalence between identifiers or records held by different authorities, carrying the asserting authority, the evidence and confidence behind the claim, and the approval, privacy and records controls that make the claim safe to publish and reuse.
model.scope_statement: WM-XCT-036 covers a single asserted equivalence (or near-equivalence) between two identified endpoints governed by different authorities, together with everything needed to judge whether that assertion may be trusted, published, disclosed and retained: the declared relation strength and its justification, the confidence attached to it, the agents who matched, published, reviewed and approved it, the authority scope and delegation under which each acted, the approval tier and any scoped exception, the privacy classification of the endpoints and of the private matching evidence, the purpose and tenant boundary within which the assertion is valid, the disclosure classes that separate a public mapping from restricted evidence, and the retention, hold, retraction and tombstone bindings for the model's own records. It is a mixin: it attaches to subject records without owning them, and it deliberately stops at the point where an external component evaluates access, enforces policy, executes destruction or stores audit trails.
in_scope: The equivalence assertion itself: subject endpoint, object endpoint, declared relation strength, justification and confidence value

Identification of the agents involved and separation of owner/steward, source authority, target authority, assertion publisher, matching operator, reviewer/adjudicator, policy authority, privacy officer and records authority
Authority scope, delegation instruments, effective and expiry times, and re-attestation triggers
Precedence between competing authorities, endpoint designation as source, alternate or historical, and the representation of a contested or refuted assertion
Approval tiers keyed to relation strength and evidence class, including reviewer independence requirements and re-approval triggers
Scoped, time-boxed and reviewable exceptions that never silently strengthen relation semantics
Privacy classification of endpoints, labels and matching features, including special-category data, protected identity and protected location, and pseudonymisation state
Declared purposes, excluded purposes, lawful-basis references, tenant and compartment scope, and cross-tenant reuse bindings
Disclosure classes separating the public mapping from private evidence, features and reviewer notes, and the scope levels (bundle, layer, finding, artifact) at which each may be released
Retention class, disposition authority citation, hold state, retraction, tombstone content and preserved provenance for this model's own records
out_of_scope: Runtime authorization: evaluating an access request and returning permit or deny is performed by an external policy decision point; this model publishes attributes and required obligations only
Policy enforcement, obligation execution and interception of requests, which belong to an external policy enforcement point
Audit capture, audit storage, audit protection and audit retention; only audit event references are carried
Physical deletion, destruction, media sanitisation and transfer of records, which the referenced records model or the adopting Dimension's records authority executes
Lifecycle of the mapped endpoints themselves: minting, updating, merging, deprecating or retiring the identifiers and records that the assertion links
Entity-resolution algorithm design, model training, feature engineering and score calibration internals of the matching operator's tooling
Reasoning and entailment over equivalence relations, including transitive closure computation and consequence materialisation
Consent capture, data protection impact assessments, records of processing activities and data subject request handling, which are owned by the referenced privacy model
Credential issuance, key management, signature suite selection and holder-side presentation protocols
Master data management survivorship, golden-record construction and downstream record merge behaviour

boundary_notes.neighbor: Authorization policy, decision and enforcement (XACML / ABAC architecture)
boundary_notes.distinction: XACML separates the policy administration point that authors policy, the policy decision point that evaluates it, the policy information point that supplies attributes and the policy enforcement point that acts on the decision. This model behaves as a policy information point and a source of declared obligations: it states the disclosure class, purpose, tenant and sensitivity attributes of an assertion. It never renders an authorization decision and never enforces one.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Mapping semantics defined by external vocabularies (SKOS, OWL)
boundary_notes.distinction: SKOS defines exactMatch, closeMatch, relatedMatch and the hierarchical match properties, and deliberately makes closeMatch non-transitive to avoid compound errors when chaining mappings. This model consumes the declared predicate as an input to approval tiering; it does not redefine predicate semantics, entailment or transitivity, and any use of those vocabularies is an alignment rather than a conformance claim.

Retention schedules, disposition authorities, freezes and destruction are administered by a records programme covering capture, maintenance and use, disposal, transfer, metadata and reporting. This model binds each of its own records to a retention class and hold reference and preserves a tombstone; the records authority approves the schedule and executes disposition.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Privacy programme (lawful basis, consent, impact assessment, data subject rights)
boundary_notes.distinction: The controller is responsible for demonstrating compliance with the processing principles and holds the lawful-basis, consent and records-of-processing artefacts. This model carries purpose codes, special-category flags and references to those artefacts so that assertions can be scoped and suppressed, but it does not capture consent, run assessments or adjudicate data subject requests.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Mapping interchange formats and mapping-set publication (SSSOM)
boundary_notes.distinction: SSSOM defines the interchange slots for mappings and mapping sets, requiring only predicate and justification while leaving author, reviewer, licence and confidence optional. This model aligns its role and evidence attributes to those slots for interoperability but applies stricter local approval rules; the serialisation, propagation and chaining rules of the interchange format remain owned there.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Selective disclosure and credential presentation infrastructure
boundary_notes.distinction: Verifiable credential ecosystems place selective and unlinkable disclosure with the holder who constructs a presentation from issued credentials. This model declares which disclosure class each part of an assertion belongs to and what handling obligation travels with it; where a mapping is presented as a credential, the presentation mechanics, proof formats and unlinkability guarantees belong to that external model.

sources.title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
sources.relevance: Supplies the agent, attribution, delegation and role vocabulary used to separate authority roles (prov:Agent, prov:wasAttributedTo, prov:qualifiedAttribution, prov:actedOnBehalfOf, prov:Delegation, prov:hadRole) and the invalidation and revision terms used for retraction and supersession (prov:wasInvalidatedBy, prov:invalidatedAtTime, prov:wasRevisionOf).

sources.title: A Simple Standard for Sharing Ontology Mappings (SSSOM) — Data Model
sources.version_or_date: SSSOM 1.1 data model specification, accessed 4 September 2026
sources.relevance: Normative slot list distinguishing author_id, creator_id, curator_id and reviewer_id, plus mapping_justification and predicate_id as mandatory, and confidence, curation_rule, mapping_provider, licence, mapping_set_version and publication_date as optional; the basis for separating assertion publisher, matching operator and reviewer and for treating evidence as first-class.

sources.title: A Simple Standard for Sharing Ontological Mappings (SSSOM)
sources.organization: Database: The Journal of Biological Databases and Curation (Oxford University Press)
sources.relevance: Peer-reviewed statement of the harm caused by unqualified mappings — non-transparent inaccuracy, missing provenance and attribution, and safety consequences of wrong equivalences — which justifies graduated approval thresholds and mandatory evidence capture.

sources.title: Person — FHIR Release 5
sources.relevance: Person.link with an assurance element qualifies confidence in an asserted cross-organisation link, explicitly tying a probabilistic match to the weakest level and a government-issued photo ID to a stronger level; also states that such records must be protected as identifying information and that inspecting a linked reference can itself reveal sensitive facts.

sources.title: Linkage — FHIR Release 5
sources.relevance: Defines an equivalence assertion held separately from the linked records, with an author that establishes the context for evaluating the linkage, an active flag for withdrawal, and item types source, alternate and historical that designate which endpoint is authoritative.

sources.title: Security Labels — FHIR Release 5
sources.relevance: Confidentiality, sensitivity and compartment codes, purpose-of-use values, obligation and refrain policies such as mask, redact and no-disclosure-without-consent, and the break-the-glass pattern with its audit requirement; grounds sensitivity labelling, tenant compartments and emergency release.

sources.title: eXtensible Access Control Markup Language (XACML) Version 3.0
sources.relevance: Normative separation of policy administration point, policy decision point, policy information point and policy enforcement point, plus obligations that a PEP must perform and advice it may ignore; establishes that this model may supply attributes and obligation references but must not evaluate or enforce.

sources.title: NIST Special Publication 800-162, Guide to Attribute Based Access Control (ABAC) Definition and Considerations
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
sources.relevance: Defines access control by evaluating subject, object, operation and environment attributes and the trust required in attribute sources; supports treating this model's privacy, purpose and tenant values as governed attributes consumed by an external decision engine.

sources.title: NIST Special Publication 800-53 Revision 5, Security and Privacy Controls for Information Systems and Organizations
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
sources.relevance: Control catalogue for access enforcement (AC-3), separation of duties (AC-5), least privilege (AC-6), event logging and audit protection (AU-2, AU-9), information management and retention (SI-12) and the privacy family covering authority to process and processing purposes (PT-2, PT-3); grounds least privilege, duty separation, retention binding and the externality of audit.

sources.title: Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (United Kingdom General Data Protection Regulation), Article 5 — Principles relating to processing of personal data
sources.version_or_date: Regulation of 27 April 2016, article text as published on legislation.gov.uk, accessed 4 September 2026
sources.relevance: Purpose limitation, data minimisation, accuracy, storage limitation, integrity and confidentiality, and the controller's accountability to demonstrate compliance; the legal basis for declared purposes, retention justification and correction of inaccurate assertions about people.

sources.title: Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (United Kingdom General Data Protection Regulation), Article 9 — Processing of special categories of personal data
sources.version_or_date: Regulation of 27 April 2016, article text as published on legislation.gov.uk, accessed 4 September 2026
sources.relevance: Enumerates the special categories — racial or ethnic origin, political opinions, religious or philosophical beliefs, trade union membership, genetic data, biometric data for identification, health, sex life and sexual orientation — that an equivalence assertion may reveal, and the narrow conditions under which such processing is permitted.

sources.title: Universal Electronic Records Management (ERM) Requirements
sources.organization: U.S. National Archives and Records Administration (NARA)
sources.relevance: Groups electronic records requirements into capture, maintenance and use, disposal, transfer, metadata and reporting, and separates programme (policy) obligations from system obligations; supports binding a retention class and disposition authority locally while the records programme executes disposal and transfer.

sources.title: Verifiable Credentials Data Model v2.0
sources.relevance: Defines selective disclosure as fine-grained holder control over what is shared, unlinkable disclosure, validity periods and credential status, and privacy guidance on data minimisation and identifier correlatability; grounds disclosure classes and the correlation risk of publishing a mapping.

sources.title: ODRL Information Model 2.2
sources.relevance: Permission, prohibition, duty, constraint, assigner and assignee parties, and the conflict property with perm, prohibit and invalid strategies; a precedent for declaring rules and conflict handling declaratively while leaving enforcement and evaluation outside the information model.

sources.title: SKOS Simple Knowledge Organization System Reference
sources.relevance: Mapping properties exactMatch, closeMatch, relatedMatch, broadMatch and narrowMatch with graduated confidence language, and the explicit decision to keep closeMatch non-transitive to avoid compound errors when chaining mappings across schemes; the standards basis for graduating approval by relation strength.

sources.title: Data Privacy Vocabulary (DPV) version 2.2
sources.organization: W3C Data Privacy Vocabularies and Controls Community Group (DPVCG)
sources.version_or_date: Version 2.2, Final Community Group Report, 31 October 2025
sources.relevance: Machine-readable taxonomies for purpose, personal data and special-category personal data, legal basis and consent states, controller and processor roles, technical and organisational measures including access control and pseudonymisation, and storage condition and processing duration for retention expression. Not a W3C Standard, so used as an alignment vocabulary only.

sources.title: The sameAs Problem: A Survey on Identity Management in the Web of Data
sources.organization: Université Paris-Saclay and Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam (arXiv preprint 1907.10528)
sources.relevance: Documents that identity assertions in open data are frequently misused and that incorrect identity has wide-ranging effects across a linked knowledge space; used as a counterexample source that motivates independent review of strict identity claims rather than as normative support.

sources.title: ValueSet: IdentityAssuranceLevel — FHIR Release 5
sources.relevance: Four graduated codes describing confidence in an asserted identity, from little or no confidence through some, high and very high confidence; a published, citable tier scale that approval thresholds can align to instead of inventing one.

bundles.name: Authority, Delegation and Approval Control
bundles.description: Who may assert, review and approve an equivalence between identifiers governed by different parties; how their authority is scoped, delegated and time-bounded; how competing authorities are ordered; and what approval an assertion needs before it may be published at a given relation strength.
bundles.rationale: An equivalence assertion is an act by an agent about identifiers that the agent may not govern. Provenance standards require attribution and delegation to be recorded explicitly, mapping standards separate author, creator, curator and reviewer, and healthcare linkage standards make the asserting author the context for evaluating the link. Without an explicit authority and approval layer, a probabilistic guess and an evidence-backed identity claim are indistinguishable once published.

layers.name: Authority Roles, Delegation and Precedence
layers.description: The separated control roles that may act on an assertion, the instruments and time windows that grant their authority, and the rules that order competing or contested authority claims.

findings.name: Separated control roles, delegation instruments and authority windows
findings.description: Distinguishes the control roles that may act on an alias assertion — owner/steward, source authority, target authority, assertion publisher, matching operator, reviewer/adjudicator, policy authority, privacy officer and records authority — and for each records the holding agent, the party on whose behalf it acts, the instrument delegating the authority, the scope of that authority and the instant at which it lapses or requires re-attestation. It also records which role pairs may not be held by the same agent for the same assertion.

questions.text: Which agent holds each control role for this assertion, and are those roles held by distinct agents?
answer_data: Role code drawn from the model's control-role code list
Identifier of the holding agent (person, organisation or software agent)
Flag recording whether the required distinctness between roles is satisfied

questions.text: On whose behalf does each role holder act, and which instrument delegates that authority?
answer_data: Identifier of the delegating agent
Reference to the delegation instrument or mandate record
Qualified delegation entry naming delegate, delegator and role

questions.text: When does each role assignment take effect, and when does it expire or require re-attestation?
answer_data: Effective time of the role assignment
Expiry time or re-attestation due time
Observation time at which this model captured the assignment

questions.text: Which namespace, tenant or identifier range does each authority cover, and what lies explicitly outside it?
answer_data: Authority scope expression (namespace, prefix, tenant or identifier range)
Explicit exclusions from that scope
Reference to the register that publishes the scope

questions.text: Which role combinations are prohibited for the same agent acting on the same assertion?
answer_data: Incompatible role pairs, for example matching operator and reviewer
Reference to the separation-of-duties rule that forbids the pair
Recorded outcome when an incompatible combination is detected

data_elements.name: Control role code
data_elements.description: Coded control role held in relation to an assertion, from the model's role list (owner/steward, source authority, target authority, assertion publisher, matching operator, reviewer, policy authority, privacy officer, records authority).

data_elements.name: Role holder reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the agent holding the role, resolvable in the adopting Dimension's agent register.

data_elements.name: Delegation instrument reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the mandate, contract or attestation under which the holder acts on behalf of another agent.

data_elements.name: Authority effective time
data_elements.description: Instant from which the role assignment is valid, recorded as an event time distinct from the ingestion time of the record.

data_elements.name: Authority expiry or re-attestation time
data_elements.description: Instant at which the role assignment lapses or must be re-attested; absence means the assignment is open-ended and subject to periodic review.

data_elements.name: Authority scope expression
data_elements.description: Declared namespace, identifier range, tenant or subject class over which the role holder's authority applies, with explicit exclusions.

data_elements.name: Incompatible role pair
data_elements.description: Pair of control roles that must not be held by the same agent for the same assertion, expressing separation of duties.

artifacts.name: Authority delegation instrument
artifacts.description: Attested record that names the delegating authority, the delegate, the role, the scope of authority and its expiry, and that is cited by every assertion the delegate publishes under it.
media_or_form: Structured attestation record in an authority register
Registry entry with delegator, delegate, role, scope and expiry
artifacts.identity_strategy: Use the authoritative identifier issued by the mandate or authority register that governs the instrument; if none exists, use a governed IRI in the delegating authority's namespace; only if neither exists, mint a UUID or ULID in the adopting Dimension. A signing date is never used as the identifier.

findings.name: Endpoint authority designation, precedence and contest
findings.description: How competing authority claims over the same equivalence are ordered: which linked endpoint is designated authoritative source, which is alternate and which is historical; whether a publisher may assert equivalence over identifiers it does not govern and what acknowledgement each endpoint authority gives; which precedence rule resolves conflicting assertions; and how a contested or refuted assertion is represented without silently changing its declared relation strength.

questions.text: Which linked endpoint is designated authoritative source, which is alternate and which is historical?
answer_data: Endpoint role code (source, alternate, historical)
Identifier of the authority governing each endpoint
Reference to the register in which the designation is published

questions.text: May a publisher assert equivalence over identifiers it does not govern, and what acknowledgement is required from each endpoint authority?
answer_data: Identifier of the asserting party
Acknowledgement state per endpoint authority (unsolicited, notified, acknowledged, disputed)
Condition under which an unacknowledged assertion may still be published

questions.text: Which precedence rule resolves conflicting assertions from different authorities, and what is recorded when no rule applies?
answer_data: Reference to the applicable precedence rule
Selected outcome (source authority prevails, later assertion prevails, both retained as unresolved)
Recorded reason when no rule applies

questions.text: What states may a contested assertion occupy, and does an open contest suspend downstream use?
answer_data: Contest state value (uncontested, contested, refuted, resolved)
Reference to the contest record and the contesting authority
Suspension flag and the disclosure consequence of suspension

questions.text: Does an assertion inherit authority when it is chained through another party's equivalence, and how is that inheritance limited?
answer_data: Chain propagation flag and the maximum chain depth permitted
Identifier of each intermediate assertion relied upon
Declared relation strength ceiling applied to a chained assertion

data_elements.name: Endpoint authority role code
data_elements.description: Designation of a linked endpoint as authoritative source, alternate representation or historical representation of the same real-world subject.

data_elements.name: Asserting party reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the agent that published the assertion and therefore supplies the context in which the link is to be evaluated.

data_elements.name: Endpoint acknowledgement state
data_elements.description: State of each endpoint authority's response to the assertion: unsolicited, notified, acknowledged or disputed.

data_elements.name: Precedence rule reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the declared rule that orders competing assertions, analogous to a declared conflict strategy in a rights policy.

data_elements.name: Contest record reference
data_elements.description: Reference to a contest or refutation raised by an endpoint authority or third party, with the contest state it produced.

data_elements.name: Chain propagation limit
data_elements.description: Maximum number of intermediate assertions through which authority may be inherited, and the relation strength ceiling applied to chained results.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Endpoint designation, acknowledgement state, precedence rule reference and contest state are inline reference values carried on the assertion record itself; they are read as attributes by consumers and by an external decision point rather than published as a standalone document. The documents that do result from a contest — the reviewer's adjudication and any retraction — are produced under the approval and records findings, so declaring a separate artifact here would duplicate them and create two competing sources of truth for one decision.

layers.name: Approval Thresholds and Scoped Exceptions
layers.description: The graduated evidence and review required before an assertion may be published at a given relation strength, and the narrow, time-boxed exceptions to that requirement.

findings.name: Approval tiers keyed to relation strength and evidence class
findings.description: Binds each declared relation strength — strict identity, curated exact match, curated close or related match, local alias, unreviewed candidate hint — to a minimum evidence class, a minimum reviewer independence and an approval tier. Strict identity claims require documentary or authority-issued evidence and a reviewer independent of the matching operator and the publisher; weaker relations may be self-approved by the publisher and must then carry the weaker relation strength. It also records what is captured when an approval is refused or an assertion is downgraded, and which changes force re-review.

questions.text: What evidence class is minimally sufficient to approve each declared relation strength?
answer_data: Declared relation strength tier
Minimum evidence class (authority-issued document, deterministic key match, curated lexical match, probabilistic score only)
Coded justification recorded with the assertion

questions.text: Which approvals require a reviewer independent of the matching operator and the publisher, and how is that independence demonstrated?
answer_data: Reviewer independence requirement per approval tier
Identifier of the reviewing agent and of the matching operator
Result of the separation-of-duties check performed before approval is recorded

questions.text: How is a numeric confidence value interpreted for approval, and who sets and periodically reviews that threshold?
answer_data: Confidence value and the scale on which it was produced
Threshold value per approval tier and the authority that set it
Date of last threshold review and the review cadence

questions.text: What is recorded when an approval is granted, refused or downgraded to a weaker relation?
answer_data: Approval decision code (approved, refused, downgraded, deferred)
Resulting relation strength and assurance level after the decision
Reason text and reference to the evidence considered

questions.text: Which changes to the endpoints, the evidence or the matching method invalidate an existing approval?
answer_data: Trigger list (endpoint deprecation, evidence withdrawal, tool or version change, threshold change)
State to which the assertion returns when a trigger fires
Deadline by which re-review must complete

data_elements.name: Declared relation strength tier
data_elements.description: The strength of the asserted relation as declared by the publisher, used as the governing input to approval requirements; graduated in the manner of exact, close and related mapping properties.

data_elements.name: Required evidence class
data_elements.description: Minimum class of evidence that must be present for the declared relation strength to be approved, from authority-issued documentary evidence down to probabilistic score only.

data_elements.name: Assurance level code
data_elements.description: Graduated confidence in the asserted identity, aligned to a published four-level assurance scale ranging from little or no confidence to very high confidence.

data_elements.name: Approval confidence threshold
data_elements.description: Numeric threshold on the reported confidence value below which the corresponding approval tier may not be granted, together with the scale it applies to.

data_elements.name: Approval tier code
data_elements.description: Required approval route: publisher self-approval, steward approval, or independent review with adjudication.

data_elements.name: Approval decision code
data_elements.description: Outcome recorded by the reviewer or adjudicator: approved, refused, downgraded to a weaker relation, or deferred pending evidence.

data_elements.name: Re-approval trigger
data_elements.description: Condition whose occurrence invalidates an existing approval and returns the assertion to a pending state.

artifacts.name: Approval threshold schedule
artifacts.description: Versioned schedule binding each relation strength tier to its required evidence class, confidence threshold, reviewer independence requirement and approval tier; published by the policy authority and cited by every approval decision.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Use the authoritative identifier issued by the policy authority's document register; if absent, use a governed IRI in the publishing authority's policy namespace with an explicit version segment; only if neither exists, mint a ULID in the adopting Dimension. Version labels are separate from the identifier and an effective date is never the identifier.

artifacts.name: Review decision record
artifacts.description: One record per review event, naming the reviewing agent, the independence check performed, the evidence considered, the decision and the resulting relation strength and assurance level.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Use the authoritative identifier issued by the review register that owns the decision; if absent, use a governed IRI in the reviewing organisation's namespace; only if neither exists, mint a ULID. Sequence position within a register is a label, not the identifier.

findings.name: Scoped, time-boxed and reviewable approval exceptions
findings.description: An exception permits an assertion to be created or kept in use without the evidence or review its declared relation strength normally requires. Each exception names the requester, the granting policy authority, the exact scope, the mandatory expiry instant, any compensating condition and the post-hoc review due date. An exception may relax an approval requirement; it may never raise the declared relation strength, the recorded assurance level or the evidence class of the assertion it covers, and its presence remains visible on the assertion.

questions.text: Which conditions justify granting an exception, and which authority alone may grant it?
answer_data: Coded exception reason (operational continuity, evidence unavailable, regulatory instruction, pilot)
Identifier of the granting policy authority and the mandate relied upon
Identifier of the requesting agent

questions.text: What is the maximum duration of an exception, and what happens automatically when it expires?
answer_data: Mandatory expiry instant of the exception
Maximum permitted duration for that exception class
Default state the assertion returns to at expiry, such as pending re-review or suspended

questions.text: What must remain unchanged in the assertion while an exception is in force?
answer_data: Invariant attributes (relation strength, assurance level, evidence class, justification)
Visibility rule requiring the exception to be disclosed with the assertion
Rejection outcome recorded if a strengthening change is attempted

questions.text: Who reviews granted exceptions after the fact, on what cadence, and what must that review reference?
answer_data: Reviewing role and review due date
Review cadence for the exception class
References the review must cite: the exception record, the covered assertions and any audit event references

data_elements.name: Exception reason code
data_elements.description: Coded justification for granting the exception, drawn from a closed list maintained by the policy authority.

data_elements.name: Granting authority reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the policy authority that granted the exception and to the mandate under which it acted.

data_elements.name: Exception scope expression
data_elements.description: Precise scope of the exception: the assertions, namespaces, tenants or relation strengths it covers, and everything it does not.

data_elements.name: Exception expiry time
data_elements.description: Mandatory instant at which the exception ceases to have effect; an exception without an expiry is invalid.

data_elements.name: Compensating condition
data_elements.description: Duty attached to the exception that must be discharged while it is in force, such as restricted disclosure, additional monitoring or mandatory notification.

data_elements.name: Exception review due date
data_elements.description: Date by which the post-hoc review of the granted exception must be completed.

artifacts.name: Exception and waiver record
artifacts.description: One record per granted exception, carrying requester, granting authority, reason, scope, expiry, compensating conditions and review due date, and cited by every assertion that relies on it.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Use the authoritative identifier issued by the exception register of the granting authority; if absent, use a governed IRI in that authority's namespace; only if neither exists, mint a ULID in the adopting Dimension. The grant date is metadata, never the identifier.

bundles.name: Privacy, Disclosure and Records Control
bundles.description: How an equivalence assertion is classified for privacy, bounded by purpose and tenant, split into public and restricted disclosure classes, and bound to retention, hold, retraction and provenance-preservation rules — while leaving decision, enforcement, deletion and audit storage to external components.
bundles.rationale: Linking two identifiers can reveal more than either identifier alone: it can defeat a pseudonym, expose a special category of personal data or reveal a protected location, and standards for cross-organisation person linking already warn that inspecting a linked reference can disclose sensitive facts. Data protection law requires purpose limitation, minimisation, accuracy and storage limitation with demonstrable accountability, and records programmes require a disposition authority and hold discipline. This bundle supplies the classifications, scopes and bindings needed to satisfy those obligations without absorbing the systems that execute them.

layers.name: Privacy Classification, Purpose and Tenant Scope
layers.description: Classification of the identifiers, labels and matching features as personal, special-category, protected-identity or protected-location data, and the declared purposes, lawful-basis references and tenant boundaries within which the assertion may be used.

findings.name: Personal, special-category, protected-identity and protected-location content
findings.description: Classifies each endpoint identifier, label, matching feature and reviewer note as personal data or not, flags any special category revealed by the link, records pseudonymisation state, and marks protected identity or protected location exposure. The controlling concern is emergent: an equivalence can defeat a pseudonym or reveal a sensitive affiliation even when neither endpoint does so alone, so the classification of the assertion is not simply the union of the endpoint classifications.

questions.text: Which elements of this assertion are personal data, and which of them reveal a special category?
answer_data: Per-element personal data flag covering identifiers, labels, features and notes
Special category codes revealed, such as health, biometric, genetic, religious or trade union affiliation
Reference to the lawful basis or special-category condition relied upon

questions.text: Does linking these endpoints defeat a pseudonym or reveal a protected identity that neither endpoint reveals alone?
answer_data: Pseudonymisation state of each endpoint
Re-identification effect assessment for the link itself
Mitigation applied, such as withholding the link, masking an endpoint or restricting the audience

questions.text: Does the assertion expose a protected or restricted location, and at what granularity may that location be disclosed?
answer_data: Protected location flag and the protection scheme relied upon
Maximum disclosable granularity, such as region rather than address
Compartment or audience permitted to receive the finer granularity

questions.text: How is an inaccurate or objected-to assertion about a person corrected or suppressed, and within what period?
answer_data: Correction or suppression route and the role that initiates it
Target period for completing the correction
Reference to the privacy model record that owns the underlying subject request

questions.text: How do the sensitivity labels of the two endpoints combine into the label carried by the assertion?
answer_data: Combination rule, such as taking the most restrictive endpoint label
Resulting confidentiality and sensitivity labels on the assertion
Additional label added because of the emergent effect of linking

data_elements.name: Personal data flag
data_elements.description: Whether the assertion or an identified part of it constitutes personal data relating to an identified or identifiable natural person.

data_elements.name: Special category code
data_elements.description: Coded special category of personal data that the assertion reveals, drawn from the categories enumerated in data protection law.

data_elements.name: Confidentiality label
data_elements.description: Graduated confidentiality classification carried by the assertion, aligned to a published confidentiality code system.

data_elements.name: Sensitivity label
data_elements.description: Non-hierarchical sensitivity marking supporting finer-grained handling than confidentiality alone.

data_elements.name: Pseudonymisation state
data_elements.description: Whether an endpoint identifier is a direct identifier, a pseudonym, or a pseudonym whose linkage key is held separately, and whether the assertion reverses that pseudonymisation.

data_elements.name: Protected location exposure flag
data_elements.description: Whether the assertion exposes a location under a protection scheme, together with the maximum granularity that may be disclosed.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Privacy classification here is a set of labels and flags carried on the assertion and on each evidence element so that an external decision point can act on them as attributes; they are inline values, not a document. The documents that would otherwise be tempting to place here — the impact assessment, the lawful-basis record and the data subject request file — are owned by the referenced privacy model, and reproducing them would give this mixin ownership of privacy programme records it does not administer.

findings.name: Declared purpose, lawful basis reference and tenant isolation
findings.description: Records the purposes for which the equivalence may be used, the purposes explicitly excluded, the reference to the authority or lawful basis permitting the processing, and the tenant or compartment inside which the assertion is valid. Cross-tenant reuse is never inherited: it requires an explicit binding naming the receiving tenant, the purpose it may serve and the authority that permitted it.

questions.text: For which declared purposes may this equivalence be used, and which uses are explicitly excluded?
answer_data: Declared purpose codes
Explicitly excluded purpose codes
Reference to the notice or agreement in which the purposes were specified

questions.text: Which authority or lawful basis permits processing these identifiers for the declared purpose, and where is that record held?
answer_data: Lawful basis or authority-to-process reference
Identifier of the controller accountable for demonstrating compliance
Location of the record of processing in the referenced privacy model

questions.text: Within which tenant, compartment or community is this assertion valid, and what is required to use it outside that boundary?
answer_data: Tenant scope reference and any compartment codes
Cross-tenant binding requirement and the authority that must grant it
Behaviour when an assertion is encountered outside its tenant scope

questions.text: How is a request to use the equivalence for a purpose that was not originally declared assessed and recorded?
answer_data: Compatibility assessment outcome for the new purpose
Deciding authority and the date of the decision
Resulting change to the declared or excluded purpose list

data_elements.name: Declared purpose code
data_elements.description: Coded purpose for which the equivalence assertion may be processed, drawn from a governed purpose taxonomy.

data_elements.name: Excluded purpose code
data_elements.description: Purpose for which use of the assertion is explicitly forbidden, expressed so that a decision point can act on it.

data_elements.name: Lawful basis or authority-to-process reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the externally held record establishing the authority or legal basis for processing the identifiers involved.

data_elements.name: Tenant scope reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the tenant, organisation or data space within which the assertion is valid and beyond which it must not be resolved by default.

data_elements.name: Compartment code
data_elements.description: Marking that restricts the assertion to a defined community, project or care setting inside the tenant.

data_elements.name: Cross-tenant binding reference
data_elements.description: Explicit binding permitting a named other tenant to use the assertion for a named purpose, with the granting authority and validity window.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Purpose codes, exclusions, tenant scope and compartment markings are scoping parameters attached to the assertion and consumed as attributes by an external decision point; they generate no document of their own. The instruments they point at — the privacy notice, the lawful-basis record, the records of processing and any data sharing agreement — are held and versioned by the referenced privacy and agreement models, so this finding carries references and subject-specific parameters only.

layers.name: Disclosure Separation and Access Scoping
layers.description: Separation of the publishable equivalence statement from restricted matching evidence, features and reviewer material, the scope levels at which each may be released, and the declarations an external decision point consumes.

findings.name: Public mapping, restricted evidence and access scoping declarations
findings.description: Splits an assertion into disclosure classes — the public equivalence statement, the private matching evidence and features, the reviewer notes, and reviewer identity — and declares for each which audience may receive it, at which scope level (bundle, layer, finding or artifact), with which handling obligation such as masking or redaction, and under which emergency release condition. Every declaration is an attribute or obligation statement consumed by an external decision and enforcement point; this model publishes no permit or deny result and executes no enforcement.

questions.text: Which parts of the assertion are publishable, and which remain restricted evidence or reviewer material?
answer_data: Disclosure class per part (public statement, restricted evidence, restricted features, reviewer notes)
Default class applied when none is declared
Audience codes permitted for each class

questions.text: At which scope — bundle, layer, finding or artifact — is each restricted part released, and what is the smallest grant that meets a legitimate need?
answer_data: Scope level at which the grant is expressed
Minimum grant satisfying the stated need, expressing least privilege
Operations permitted at that scope, such as read of metadata only

questions.text: Is the reviewer's identity published with the decision, pseudonymised or withheld, and what condition reveals it?
answer_data: Reviewer visibility mode (published, pseudonymised, withheld)
Condition and authority under which the identity may be revealed
Audience entitled to the revealed identity

questions.text: Who may invoke emergency release of restricted evidence, which purpose of use must be declared, and when does that grant lapse?
answer_data: Roles entitled to invoke emergency release
Purpose-of-use value that must accompany the invocation
Lapse instant of the grant and the mandatory post-hoc review reference

questions.text: What does this model publish in place of an allow or deny result, and which component consumes it?
answer_data: Attribute set published for the decision point (classification, purpose, tenant, disclosure class)
Obligation references that an enforcement point must discharge, such as mask or redact
Identifier of the external decision point relied upon

data_elements.name: Disclosure class code
data_elements.description: Class assigned to each part of the assertion determining whether it is publishable or restricted: public statement, restricted evidence, restricted feature, reviewer note or reviewer identity.

data_elements.name: Audience code
data_elements.description: Audience permitted to receive a given disclosure class, such as public, tenant member, endpoint authority, reviewer, regulator or data subject.

data_elements.name: Grant scope level
data_elements.description: Level at which a disclosure grant is expressed: bundle, layer, finding or artifact.

data_elements.name: Handling obligation code
data_elements.description: Obligation that travels with a disclosure, such as mask, redact, encrypt, no onward disclosure without consent or no reuse.

data_elements.name: Reviewer visibility mode
data_elements.description: Whether the reviewing agent's identity is published with the decision, pseudonymised, or withheld pending a named condition.

data_elements.name: Emergency release descriptor
data_elements.description: Declaration of who may invoke emergency release, what it unlocks, the purpose of use it must declare, its lapse instant and the review it triggers.

data_elements.name: External decision point reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the authorization decision point that consumes these declarations; recorded so that the boundary of responsibility is explicit and resolvable.

artifacts.name: Disclosure profile
artifacts.description: Versioned declarative profile mapping disclosure class by audience and scope level to the permitted projection and the handling obligations that accompany it; published by the owner package and read by the external decision and enforcement points. It is a declaration of what may be released, never a record of a decision taken.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Use the authoritative identifier issued by the owner package's document register; if absent, use a governed IRI in the publishing Dimension's policy namespace including an explicit version segment; only if neither exists, mint a ULID. Effective dates and version labels are attributes, not identifiers.

layers.name: Retention, Hold, Retraction and Provenance Preservation
layers.description: Binding of this model's own records to a retention class and disposition authority, the hold discipline that suspends disposition, and the retraction and tombstone rules that keep withdrawal detectable while preserving provenance.

findings.name: Retention class, disposition authority citation and hold state
findings.description: Binds each record this model owns — the assertion, its evidence, the review decision and the exception record — to a retention class and a citation of the disposition authority that governs it, and records the current hold state with the agent that applied it and the instant it took effect. The binding and the hold reference live here; approving the schedule, executing destruction or transfer, and lifting a hold are performed by the records authority.

questions.text: Which retention class and disposition authority govern the assertion, its evidence and its review record?
answer_data: Retention class code per record kind
Citation of the approved disposition authority
Retention period start event, such as approval or last use

questions.text: What is the current hold state, who applied it, and what evidence is required to lift it?
answer_data: Hold state value (none, applied, lifted)
Identifier of the applying authority and the event time of application
Reference to the hold notice and the condition for lifting it

questions.text: May private evidence be disposed of earlier than the published mapping, and what must survive that disposal?
answer_data: Separate retention classes for evidence and for the published statement
Minimum surviving record after evidence disposal, such as justification code and approval reference
Effect on the assertion's assurance level once supporting evidence is gone

questions.text: Which system executes destruction or transfer, and what remains in this model afterwards?
answer_data: Identifier of the executing records system or programme
Confirmation reference returned after disposition
Residual record retained locally, such as a tombstone and disposition citation

data_elements.name: Retention class code
data_elements.description: Coded retention class assigned to a record kind owned by this model, referencing the schedule that defines its period and disposition action.

data_elements.name: Disposition authority citation
data_elements.description: Citation of the approved authority that permits eventual disposal or transfer of the record, held as a resolvable identifier rather than reproduced text.

data_elements.name: Hold state code
data_elements.description: Whether a legal hold or freeze currently suspends disposition of the record.

data_elements.name: Hold applying authority reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the authority that applied or lifted the hold, together with the notice it relied upon.

data_elements.name: Hold effective time
data_elements.description: Event time at which the hold took effect, recorded separately from the time this model ingested the hold notice.

data_elements.name: Evidence retention class code
data_elements.description: Retention class applied specifically to private matching evidence, features and reviewer notes, which may be shorter than that of the published statement.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Retention class, disposition authority citation and hold state are reference values bound to records this model owns; the governing documents — the approved retention schedule, the disposition authority instrument and the hold or freeze notice — are created, versioned and executed by the records authority. Reproducing them locally would create a second, unauthoritative copy of a records-programme artifact and would imply that this model can approve or lift a hold, which it cannot.

findings.name: Retraction, tombstone content and preserved provenance
findings.description: Withdrawal of an assertion is an event, not an erasure: it produces a retraction record naming the retracting authority, the reason and the event time, and leaves a tombstone that lets downstream consumers detect that a previously published equivalence no longer holds. The tombstone carries the assertion identifier, the retraction reason, any superseding assertion and the audit event reference, while the substantive evidence may already have been disposed of under its own retention class.

questions.text: What causes an assertion to be withdrawn, and which authority may withdraw it?
answer_data: Retraction reason code (error, refutation, endpoint retirement, legal instruction, expiry of exception)
Identifier of the retracting authority and its mandate
Event time of the retraction and its ingestion time

questions.text: What minimum record survives withdrawal so that downstream consumers can detect it?
answer_data: Retained assertion identifier and its version
Retraction status value and effective instant
Fields deliberately omitted from the tombstone for privacy reasons

questions.text: Which provenance of the withdrawn assertion must be preserved, and under whose retention rule?
answer_data: Preserved attribution: publisher, matching operator, reviewer and approval reference
Invalidating activity and the agent responsible for it
Retention class that governs the preserved provenance and any audit event reference

questions.text: Is the withdrawn assertion replaced by a corrected one, and how is that replacement expressed?
answer_data: Identifier of the superseding assertion, if any
Revision or derivation relation between the two records
Guidance to consumers on which record is now current

data_elements.name: Retraction reason code
data_elements.description: Coded reason for withdrawing the assertion, drawn from a closed list maintained by the owner package.

data_elements.name: Retraction event time
data_elements.description: Instant at which the assertion ceased to be valid, recorded separately from the instant this model ingested the retraction.

data_elements.name: Tombstone status value
data_elements.description: Status carried by the surviving record indicating that the assertion was withdrawn rather than never published.

data_elements.name: Superseding assertion reference
data_elements.description: Reference to a corrected assertion that replaces the withdrawn one, expressed as a revision relation.

data_elements.name: Preserved provenance reference
data_elements.description: References to the attribution, approval and invalidation records preserved after withdrawal, including the responsible agents.

data_elements.name: Audit event reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the audit event recorded in the external audit store for the retraction; the reference only, never the audit record itself.

artifacts.name: Retraction notice and tombstone
artifacts.description: One record per withdrawal, carrying the withdrawn assertion identifier and version, the retraction reason, the retracting authority, the event time, any superseding assertion and the preserved provenance references; published so that consumers who previously received the assertion can detect the withdrawal.
media_or_form: Tombstone entry in the assertion register
artifacts.identity_strategy: Use the authoritative identifier issued by the assertion register that owns the withdrawn record; if absent, use a governed IRI derived from the withdrawn assertion's IRI plus a retraction segment; only if neither exists, mint a ULID. The retraction date is recorded as an event time, never used as the identifier.

functions.name: Assign and attest a control role
functions.description: Record that a named agent holds a control role for a defined scope, on whose behalf it acts, under which delegation instrument, and until when.
inputs: Effective time and expiry or re-attestation time
outputs: Role assignment record with qualified delegation
Separation-of-duties check result for the affected assertions
preconditions: The delegating agent is itself recorded with authority covering the delegated scope
The delegation instrument reference resolves
The assignment does not create a forbidden role combination for an existing assertion
effects: Role assignment becomes citable by assertions created within its scope and validity window
Assignment is queued for re-attestation at its expiry time

functions.name: Determine the required approval tier for a proposed assertion
functions.description: Given the declared relation strength, the evidence class present and any confidence value, look up the approval threshold schedule and return the required approval tier and reviewer independence requirement. This determines what approval is required; it never grants approval and never authorises access.
inputs: Reference to the current approval threshold schedule
outputs: Required approval tier
Reviewer independence requirement
Shortfall statement naming any missing evidence
preconditions: A current version of the approval threshold schedule is resolvable
The declared relation strength is a value in the governed tier list
effects: Proposed assertion is placed in a pending state until the required approval or a valid exception exists

functions.name: Record a review or adjudication outcome
functions.description: Capture the reviewer's decision on a pending assertion or on a contest, including the independence check, the evidence considered, the decision and the resulting relation strength and assurance level.
inputs: Reviewer identifier and independence check result
outputs: Review decision record
Updated relation strength and assurance level on the assertion
Audit event reference returned by the external audit store
preconditions: The reviewer holds the reviewer role within a valid authority window
The reviewer is not the matching operator or the publisher when independence is required
The required evidence class for the target relation strength is present, or the decision is a downgrade or refusal
effects: Assertion moves from pending to approved, refused or downgraded
Any prior approval superseded by this decision is marked as superseded rather than deleted

functions.name: Grant a scoped, time-boxed exception
functions.description: Record an exception that relaxes an approval requirement for a named scope until a mandatory expiry, with compensating conditions and a post-hoc review date, without altering the relation strength or assurance level of any covered assertion.
inputs: Requesting agent and exception reason code
Granting policy authority and mandate reference
Scope expression and covered assertion set
Expiry time, compensating conditions and review due date
outputs: Exception record
Exception reference attached to each covered assertion
preconditions: The granting agent holds the policy authority role for the stated scope
An expiry time is supplied and is within the maximum duration for the exception class
The exception does not raise the relation strength, assurance level or evidence class of any covered assertion
effects: Covered assertions may be published while carrying a visible exception reference
At expiry the covered assertions return to the pending or suspended state defined for the exception class

functions.name: Classify privacy sensitivity of an assertion and its evidence
functions.description: Apply personal data, special category, confidentiality, sensitivity, compartment, pseudonymisation and protected-location values to the assertion and to each evidence element, including any label that arises only from the act of linking.
inputs: Endpoint identifiers, labels and their existing classifications
Applicable special category and confidentiality code lists
outputs: Classification label set on the assertion
Per-element classification on evidence, features and reviewer notes
Re-identification effect statement for the link
preconditions: The tenant scope of the assertion is known
The governing code lists for confidentiality, sensitivity and special categories are resolvable
effects: Labels become attributes available to the external decision point
Default disclosure class of each element is set from its classification

functions.name: Project a disclosure-scoped view of an assertion
functions.description: Materialise the subset of an assertion permitted for a stated audience and scope level according to the current disclosure profile, applying the declared masking or redaction obligations. The function applies a declared profile to produce a projection; it does not evaluate an access request, does not return permit or deny, and does not enforce the result.
inputs: Audience code and requested scope level
outputs: Projected assertion view limited to the permitted disclosure classes
Handling obligations attached to the projection
Statement of the classes withheld from the projection
preconditions: A current disclosure profile version is resolvable
The declared purpose of use is present in the assertion's declared purpose list, or a valid exception reference is supplied
The request has already been authorised by the external decision point
effects: A projection is produced together with its obligations for the enforcement point to discharge
An audit event reference for the disclosure is recorded against the assertion

functions.name: Bind retention class and record hold state
functions.description: Attach a retention class and disposition authority citation to a record owned by this model and record the application or lifting of a legal hold as notified by the records authority. The function records bindings and states; it never destroys, transfers or sanitises anything.
inputs: Retention class code and disposition authority citation
Hold notice reference, applying authority and hold event time
outputs: Retention binding on the record
Updated hold state with applying authority and effective time
preconditions: The retention class resolves in the schedule published by the records authority
A hold state change is accompanied by a resolvable notice reference from an authority entitled to issue it
effects: Disposition of the record is suspended while the hold state is applied
Eligibility for disposition is computed by the records system from the bound class, not by this model

functions.name: Retract an assertion and publish a tombstone
functions.description: Withdraw a previously published assertion by recording the invalidating event, publishing a retraction notice and leaving a tombstone that preserves the identifier, the reason, the responsible authority and the references needed to trace what happened.
inputs: Retraction reason code and retracting authority
outputs: Retraction notice and tombstone record
Preserved provenance references
Notification payload for prior recipients
preconditions: The retracting agent holds an authority covering the assertion's scope, or is the endpoint authority whose contest was upheld
Any legal hold on the record permits the retraction to be recorded without disposing of the underlying evidence
effects: The assertion ceases to be current and is excluded from disclosure projections other than the tombstone
Provenance, approval and exception references survive the withdrawal under their own retention classes

composition.purpose: The endpoints of an equivalence are identifiers governed elsewhere; the parent model owns identifier structure, resolution and reference semantics, while this model adds only the equivalence assertion and its governance.

composition.target: Authorization policy, decision and enforcement model (XACML / ABAC architecture)
composition.purpose: This model supplies classification, purpose, tenant and disclosure-class attributes plus obligation references and names the decision point it relies on; evaluating a request, returning permit or deny, and enforcing the result remain entirely with that model.

Restricted disclosures, exception invocations, approvals and retractions carry an audit event reference; capture, protection, retention and interrogation of audit records are owned by the audit store.

Retention class, disposition authority citation and hold state are bound to this model's records; schedule approval, freeze administration, destruction, transfer and sanitisation are executed by the records authority.

composition.target: Privacy, lawful basis and consent model
composition.purpose: Purpose codes, special-category flags and lawful-basis references are carried locally so assertions can be scoped and suppressed; consent capture, impact assessment, records of processing and data subject request handling stay with the privacy model.

composition.target: Provenance model aligned to W3C PROV
composition.purpose: Attribution, delegation, role, revision and invalidation of assertions are expressed using PROV terms so that governance history is portable; this is an alignment and no conformance to PROV constraints is claimed without evidence.

Role attributes map to author, creator, curator and reviewer slots and evidence maps to justification, curation rule and confidence so governed assertions can be exchanged as mapping sets; serialisation, propagation and chaining rules remain owned by that profile.

composition.target: HL7 FHIR Person.link and Linkage assurance profile
composition.purpose: Relation strength tiers and assurance levels align to a published four-level assurance scale and to source, alternate and historical endpoint designation for healthcare interchange; no FHIR conformance is claimed.

composition.target: Subject entity, registry or catalogue model adopting cross-authority equivalence
composition.purpose: The mixin attaches authority, approval, privacy and records controls to a host model's records without owning their identifiers, lifecycle or business semantics.

composition.target: Selective disclosure and credential presentation model
composition.purpose: Where a governed mapping is disclosed as a credential, this model states the disclosure class and handling obligations while presentation construction, proof formats and unlinkability guarantees belong to the credential model.

owner_package_requirements: Name one accountable owner or steward package for alias governance, recorded as an agent with a resolvable mandate reference, before any assertion is published.
Publish and version the approval threshold schedule and the disclosure profile; assertions may not be published while either is missing or unresolvable.
Register the external policy decision point, records authority and audit store that this model depends on; an unresolved dependency blocks publication of restricted classes.
Record a privacy officer contact and a lawful-basis reference for every assertion classified as personal data, and a records authority contact for every retention class in use.

Maintain the closed code lists for control roles, relation strength tiers, evidence classes, exception reasons, disclosure classes and retraction reasons, with supersession pointers for retired values.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Local identifiers within this model are stable lower-kebab-case slugs and are never reused. Anything published outside the model — assertions, role assignments, exceptions, retractions and profile versions — is identified by a governed IRI in a namespace controlled by the publishing authority, with CURIE prefixes declared explicitly in the exchange payload so that abbreviations cannot be resolved ambiguously. Endpoint identifiers are carried in the namespace of their own governing authority and are never rewritten into the local namespace.
registry_links: Registry entry vr.wm-xct-036 in the world-model record plane, navigation path NAV.XCT.ALS
Parent model WM-XCT-011 for identifier and reference semantics of the assertion endpoints

External code systems referenced as alignments: mapping properties from SKOS, the four-level identity assurance value set, confidentiality, sensitivity, compartment and purpose-of-use codes, and the privacy purpose and special-category taxonomies

canonicalization_rules: Expand every CURIE to its full IRI before comparison or hashing; declared prefixes are metadata and never part of the canonical form.
Order object keys and repeated values deterministically, normalise all timestamps to RFC 3339 with whole seconds and an explicit offset, and serialise confidence values at a fixed declared precision.
Exclude human labels, comments and reviewer notes from the identity hash of an assertion so that editorial changes do not create a false new version.
Treat the pair of endpoint identifiers together with the declared predicate and the asserting party as the canonical key of an assertion; direction is preserved and never normalised away.
patch_rules: Every patch carries the acting agent, a reason code, the event time of the change and the ingestion time at which it was recorded.
Changes to relation strength, evidence class, approval tier or assurance level are not patches: they require a new approval decision and a new assertion version.
Sensitivity, confidentiality and compartment labels may be strengthened by the privacy officer at any time; weakening a label requires a recorded review.
Withdrawal is expressed as a retraction record plus tombstone; no patch may remove an assertion in place.
compatibility_rules: Adding an optional governance attribute or a new code list value is a backward-compatible change and requires only a minor version increment.
Tightening an approval threshold, narrowing a disclosure class or making an attribute mandatory is breaking for consumers and requires a major version increment plus notice to known recipients.
Code list values are added and deprecated but never redefined; a deprecated value is retained with a supersession pointer so historical records stay interpretable.
Consumers must ignore unknown optional attributes and must refuse to weaken a handling obligation they do not understand.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier issued by the system of record that governs the artifact — for example the mandate register for a delegation instrument, the review register for a decision record, the exception register for a waiver, or the records system for a retention instrument.
Governed global identifier or IRI in a namespace controlled by the publishing authority, including an explicit version segment where the artifact is versioned.
UUID or ULID minted by the adopting Dimension only when neither of the above exists; a date, an effective period, a file name or a sequence label is never an identifier.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All time values are RFC 3339 timestamps carrying at least whole seconds and an explicit UTC offset or the Z designator; a bare date or a local time without offset is invalid. Event time — when the approval, exception, hold, disclosure or retraction actually took effect — is recorded separately from observation or ingestion time, which is when this model captured or was notified of the event, and the two are never substituted for one another. Where an external authority supplies only an event time, the ingestion time is still recorded locally by the receiving system.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artifacts — review decision records, exception records and retraction notices — are named as artifact kind, subject assertion identifier and a zero-padded monotonic sequence number assigned by the issuing register. The sequence is monotonic per register, never reused after withdrawal, and is a label used for ordering and display only; the identifier of the artifact is assigned by the identity priority rule and contains no date component.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Each artifact carries a content digest with its named algorithm together with the identity of the signing or attesting agent. A change of digest creates a new version entry that preserves the superseded digest and its supersession reason; superseded versions are retained under their retention class rather than overwritten. An assertion that cites an artifact must be able to resolve both the artifact identifier and the digest that was current when the citation was made.

policies: Strict identity claims require the evidence class and reviewer independence set by the approval threshold schedule; the matching operator may never approve its own output, and a self-approved assertion may only carry a weaker relation strength.

Exceptions are scoped, time-boxed, visible on every assertion that relies on them and reviewed after the fact; an exception may relax an approval requirement but may never raise relation strength, assurance level or evidence class.

Private matching evidence, features, reviewer notes and reviewer identity default to restricted; publication requires an explicit disclosure class in the current disclosure profile, and the public statement is separated from the evidence that supports it.

Alignment to external vocabularies and value sets is declared as alignment only; conformance to any external standard is asserted solely where validation evidence is recorded, and observed conflicts are logged rather than resolved silently.

This model is not an authorization decision point: it publishes attributes, disclosure classes and obligation references for an external decision and enforcement point, holds only references to audit events, and never executes destruction, transfer or sanitisation of records.

read: Reading the public equivalence statement requires only the public disclosure class; reading restricted evidence, features, reviewer notes or reviewer identity requires an explicit grant expressed at bundle, layer, finding or artifact scope.
Every read of a restricted class must present a purpose-of-use value that matches a declared purpose of the assertion, or a resolvable exception reference.
Reads are served through the declared disclosure profile as a projection carrying its handling obligations; an unprojected read of the full record is not offered by the interface.
Cross-tenant reads require an explicit cross-tenant binding; tenant scope is never inherited through a chained assertion.
create: Creating an assertion requires at minimum: both endpoint identifiers, the declared relation strength, a coded justification, the asserting party, the tenant scope and the privacy classification.
Creation is refused where the required approval tier for the declared relation strength has neither a recorded approval nor a valid, unexpired exception.
Creation is refused where the acting agent holds a role combination forbidden by the separation-of-duties rules for that assertion.
Every created record carries its event time and its ingestion time, and cites the versions of the approval threshold schedule and disclosure profile in force at creation.
update: Governance attributes — authority references, purposes, labels, tenant scope, retention class and hold state — are changed by attributed patch carrying actor, reason and event time.
Relation strength, evidence class, assurance level and approval tier are not updatable in place; changing them creates a new assertion version subject to fresh approval.
Strengthening a sensitivity or confidentiality label takes effect immediately on the privacy officer's authority; weakening one requires a recorded review by the policy authority.
Superseded values are retained with their supersession reason so that a consumer holding an earlier projection can determine what changed.
delete: Records owned by this model are never erased in place: withdrawal creates a retraction record and leaves a tombstone carrying the assertion identifier and version, the retraction reason, the retracting authority, the event time and any superseding assertion.

Each record binds a retention class and a disposition authority citation; destruction, transfer and media sanitisation are executed by the referenced records retention and disposition model or the adopting Dimension's records authority, never by this model, which only records the resulting confirmation reference.

While a hold state is applied, no disposition may proceed for the held records; applying and lifting a hold are acts of the records authority and this model records the notice reference, the applying agent and the hold event time.

Private matching evidence, features and reviewer notes may reach the end of a shorter retention class than the published statement; when they are disposed of, the surviving record retains the coded justification, the approval reference and a note that supporting evidence is no longer held.

Where a data subject seeks erasure of personal data, the referenced privacy model owns the decision and its legal exemptions; on instruction this model suppresses the assertion from all disclosure projections and retains only the minimum tombstone permitted by the applicable retention rule or legal hold.

Audit events referencing withdrawn or disposed records are retained and managed entirely by the external audit store; this model deletes nothing there and keeps only the event references it already holds.

roles.name: Owner or steward of the alias governance package
responsibilities: Hold accountability for the model's records and their quality
Publish and version the approval threshold schedule and disclosure profile
Maintain the closed code lists and the register of external dependencies

roles.name: Assertion publisher
responsibilities: Create assertions with a declared relation strength, coded justification and evidence references
Cite the delegation instrument under which it acts and notify the endpoint authorities
Withdraw its own assertions when they are shown to be wrong

roles.name: Matching operator
responsibilities: Produce candidate equivalences and record the method, tool, version and confidence value
Retain the matching evidence and features under their declared retention class
Refrain from approving its own candidates where independence is required

roles.name: Reviewer or adjudicator
responsibilities: Assess evidence against the required evidence class and record the decision with its reason
Adjudicate contests raised by endpoint authorities and record the precedence outcome
Confirm and record the independence check before an approval is entered

roles.name: Policy authority
responsibilities: Set and periodically review approval thresholds and confidence thresholds
Grant, scope, time-box and review exceptions
Own the precedence rules used to order competing assertions

roles.name: Privacy officer
responsibilities: Approve the privacy classification and the emergent re-identification assessment for linking
Maintain declared and excluded purposes and the lawful-basis references
Direct suppression or correction of assertions on instruction from the privacy model

roles.name: Records authority
responsibilities: Own retention schedules and disposition authorities cited by this model
Apply and lift holds and notify this model of the resulting state
Execute destruction and transfer and return the disposition confirmation reference

roles.name: Source and target endpoint authorities
responsibilities: Govern the identifiers being linked and their designation as source, alternate or historical
Acknowledge, dispute or refute assertions made about their identifiers
Notify deprecation or retirement of an endpoint that invalidates an approval

access.default_rule: Deny by default for matching evidence, features, reviewer notes, reviewer identity and exception records; the public equivalence statement is released only at the disclosure class and audience declared in the current disclosure profile, always with its handling obligations attached. This model states what class and obligations apply; the decision to release and its enforcement are performed by the referenced external decision and enforcement points.
